subproblem.title: Convergence of the mollified test functions against μ: ∫(∫ζ(y)ρ_j(y − z)dy)dμ(z) → ∫ζ dμ (parent Step 3)
subproblem.statement: Let N ∈ ℕ, μ a measure on ℝ^N, ζ : ℝ^N → ℝ continuous with compact support, and δ ∈ ℝ with μ(cthickening(δ, tsupport ζ)) < ∞. For j ∈ ℕ let ρ_j : ℝ^N → ℝ be continuous with ρ_j ≥ 0, ∫ ρ_j dL^N = 1 and tsupport ρ_j ⊆ B̄_{r_j}(0), where r_j ∈ ℝ satisfy r_j ≤ δ for all j and r_j → 0. Then ∫ (∫ ζ(y)ρ_j(y − z) dL^N(y)) dμ(z) → ∫ ζ dμ as j → ∞.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (N : ℕ) (μ : Measure (Rn N)) (ζ : Rn N → ℝ) (ρ : ℕ → Rn N → ℝ) (r : ℕ → ℝ) (δ : ℝ), Continuous ζ → HasCompactSupport ζ → μ (Metric.cthickening δ (tsupport ζ)) < ∞ → (∀ j, Continuous (ρ j)) → (∀ j y, 0 ≤ ρ j y) → (∀ j, ∫ y, ρ j y = 1) → (∀ j, tsupport (ρ j) ⊆ Metric.closedBall (0 : Rn N) (r j)) → (∀ j, r j ≤ δ) → Tendsto r atTop (𝓝 0) → Tendsto (fun j ↦ ∫ z, (∫ y, ζ y * ρ j (y - z)) ∂μ) atTop (𝓝 (∫ z, ζ z ∂μ))
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: parent proof Step 3 ("ζ̃_σ(z) − ζ(z) = ∫(ζ(y) − ζ(z))φ_σ(y − z)dy, so |ζ̃_σ − ζ| ≤ Kσ; also 0 ≤ ζ̃_σ ≤ M and ζ̃_σ vanishes off K'. As μ(K') < ∞, dominated convergence gives ∫ζ̃_σ dμ → ∫ζ dμ"), for general kernels ρ_j and with the Lipschitz modulus Kσ replaced by the modulus of uniform continuity of ζ. Notation: T := tsupport ζ (compact); K' := cthickening(δ, T), which is closed, hence Borel; M := sup|ζ| < ∞; ζ̃_j(z) := ∫ ζ(y)ρ_j(y − z) dy. No step uses N ≥ 1.

1. (Mass one; r_j ≥ 0.) By invariance of L^N under y ↦ y − z (integral_sub_right_eq_self), ∫ ρ_j(y − z) dy = ∫ ρ_j = 1 for every z. In particular ρ_j ≢ 0, so the set B̄_{r_j}(0) ⊇ tsupport ρ_j is non-empty, i.e. r_j ≥ 0; hence δ ≥ r_j ≥ 0 and T ⊆ K'.

2. (Support and bound.) If ζ̃_j(z) ≠ 0 there is y with ζ(y) ≠ 0 and ρ_j(y − z) ≠ 0; then y ∈ T and |y − z| ≤ r_j ≤ δ, so z ∈ K' (Metric.mem_cthickening_of_dist_le). Moreover |ζ̃_j(z)| ≤ M ∫ ρ_j(y − z) dy = M by step 1. Hence |ζ̃_j| ≤ M·1_{K'} for every j, and also |ζ| ≤ M·1_{K'} (as T ⊆ K').

3. (Measurability.) Each ζ̃_j is continuous: ρ_j is continuous with compact support (tsupport ρ_j ⊆ B̄_{r_j}(0)), hence bounded; for z_k → z the integrands y ↦ ζ(y)ρ_j(y − z_k) converge pointwise to ζ(y)ρ_j(y − z) and are dominated by (sup ρ_j)|ζ(y)|, which is integrable (ζ continuous with compact support); dominated convergence applies. Hence ζ̃_j is Borel measurable.

4. (Uniform convergence.) ζ is uniformly continuous (continuous with compact support; HasCompactSupport.uniformContinuous_of_continuous). Let ε > 0; choose η > 0 such that |ζ(y) − ζ(y')| ≤ ε whenever |y − y'| ≤ η, and j₀ such that r_j ≤ η for j ≥ j₀ (possible since r_j → 0). By step 1, ζ̃_j(z) − ζ(z) = ∫ (ζ(y) − ζ(z))ρ_j(y − z) dy, and the integrand vanishes unless |y − z| ≤ r_j. Hence for j ≥ j₀ and every z, |ζ̃_j(z) − ζ(z)| ≤ ε ∫ ρ_j(y − z) dy = ε. Thus ζ̃_j → ζ uniformly, in particular pointwise.

5. (Conclusion.) The function M·1_{K'} is μ-integrable because μ(K') < ∞; it dominates |ζ̃_j| for every j (step 2); the ζ̃_j are measurable (step 3) and converge pointwise to ζ (step 4). By the dominated convergence theorem, ∫ ζ̃_j dμ → ∫ ζ dμ. ∎
proof_key_steps: ∫ρ_j(y − z)dy = 1 for every z; hence r_j ≥ 0 and tsupport ζ ⊆ K' := cthickening(δ, tsupport ζ).
ζ̃_j(z) := ∫ζ(y)ρ_j(y − z)dy vanishes off K' and |ζ̃_j| ≤ sup|ζ|.
ζ̃_j is continuous (dominated convergence), hence measurable.
|ζ̃_j(z) − ζ(z)| ≤ the modulus of uniform continuity of ζ at r_j → 0.
Dominated convergence against μ with the bound sup|ζ|·1_{K'} ∈ L¹(μ).

audit.reason: The type matches the prose without adding positivity assumptions on ζ or the radii. Mass one forces nonnegative radii; continuity and bounded support ensure kernel integrability. Uniform continuity gives convergence, while the finite-measure thickening supplies a common integrable bound. Dominated convergence applies to the arbitrary measure μ. The proof is complete and independent.
